topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecture's scope and outlines the intended learning outcomes regarding cancer evolution and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutational clonal selection and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive competitive cellular fitness and tumor development.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and the cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and investigate how normal tissue hierarchies and specific cells of origin influence cancer initiation across tissues.

topics.label: Microenvironmental signals, inflammation, and stromal support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how inflammatory signals, environmental promoters, and supportive stromal interactions are essential to initiate and sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Techniques for investigating tumor heterogeneity and evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys single-cell sequencing, spatial profiling technologies, and computational approaches used to map tumor dynamics and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrated evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental coevolution into a comprehensive framework of malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
